rounds.text: Radix Industries is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround, evidenced by a sharp improvement in quarterly operating margins to 12% in September 2026, up from 8% in the year-ago quarter [E31]. This efficiency is bolstered by a dramatic reduction in working capital requirements from 109 days to 59.4 days [E50], ensuring that profits are fully backed by cash with a conversion ratio of 2.05x [E34]. The company maintains a fortress balance sheet with negligible debt of Rs 0.21 Cr [E38] and a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E37]. Furthermore, the firm is demonstrating accelerating profitability, with a 3-year compounded profit growth of 28% [E20] and a recent 30% year-over-year net profit increase [E55]. Conceded: the stock trades at a high P/E of 63.4x [E1] and a P/B of 8.11x [E2], while the trailing twelve-month sales growth has contracted by 15% [E17]. Despite these valuation concerns, the company’s ability to generate a 19.6% ROCE [E12] significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of 9.64% [E10], suggesting that the business is creating superior value relative to its peers.

Radix Industries is currently priced for perfection, trading at a steep P/E of 63.4x and a P/B of 8.11x, both of which significantly exceed their respective sector benchmarks of 16.85x and 1.71x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This aggressive valuation is further challenged by a reverse DCF analysis, which indicates that the current market price already demands an earnings growth rate of 24.1%, surpassing the 18.0% base case assumption [E44]. The stock’s fundamental disconnect is highlighted by a DCF model suggesting an intrinsic value of only Rs 85 per share, resulting in a substantial negative margin of safety of -56.2% [E42, E43]. Furthermore, the company’s recent performance is inconsistent, evidenced by a -15% decline in compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and an inconsistent operating margin trend [E17, E32, E33]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with minimal debt, healthy cash conversion, and recent improvements in quarterly operating margins [E31, E34, E37, E38]. Despite these operational strengths, the stock remains vulnerable, having shed 31% of its value over the last year and currently sitting at only 8% of its 52-week range [E5, E25].

The bear’s focus on high valuation multiples ignores the company’s superior capital efficiency, as evidenced by an ROA of 12.51% and ROCE of 19.6%, which significantly outperform sector benchmarks [E8, E10, E12, E66]. While the bear cites a negative margin of safety, this model fails to account for the company’s accelerating momentum, where profit growth has recently begun to outpace price growth by 36% [E42, E46]. Conceded: the P/E of 63.4x and P/B of 8.11x are high relative to sector averages [E1, E2, E6, E7]. However, the bear’s reliance on trailing twelve-month sales data ignores the most recent evidence of a turnaround, specifically the 30% year-over-year net profit increase and the 3 percentage point expansion in quarterly operating margins [E31, E55, E62]. The company’s financial health is robust, characterized by being almost debt-free and maintaining a healthy dividend payout of 28.6%, which provides a buffer that static DCF models often overlook [E37, E48, E49]. Finally, the reduction in working capital requirements from 109 days to 59.4 days demonstrates an operational efficiency that justifies a premium valuation over less agile competitors [E50].

Conceded: the company demonstrates superior ROCE of 19.6% compared to sector median of 10.4% [E12, E66]. However, invoking strong capital efficiency does not neutralize a trailing P/E of 63.4x and a P/B of 8.11x that dwarf sector benchmarks of 16.85x and 1.71x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. While the bull points to profit acceleration outstripping 1-year price growth, this sits against a 1-year share price collapse of -31% and a TTM sales contraction of -15% [E17, E25, E46]. The argument that static DCF models overlook debt-free robustness ignores the quantitative output of those models, which peg intrinsic value at Rs 85 and leave a severe margin of safety of -56.2% [E42, E43]. Furthermore, relying on recent quarterly margin expansion to justify a premium misses the reality of an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend and earnings that include Rs 1.22 Cr in other income [E31, E32, E33, E53]. Finally, a reverse DCF exposes the core valuation risk: today's price already demands a lofty 24.1% earnings growth rate, forcing the business to clear an aggressively high hurdle [E44].
